conclusions.interpretation: Nominal target range and Core Animation optical units independently affect native output. Fresh public opticalOutputScale1-to203-to1 at fixed target1000 reversibly changes compositor output on byte-identical source pixels. This corroborates the source-supported stale scale1 versus unity203 mismatch; it does not establish panel nits.

sourceAudit.finding: Pack divides absolute source nits by203; published LINEAR BT2020 metadata carries actual luminance peak.
PL_HDR_NORM unity is203 nits, matching import contract.
No preferred_csp, preferred_ref_luma or set_color callback in measured binary.
macvk auto reference white is0; LINEAR source gets LINEAR hint, but no external target parameters restore its range.
Linear format maps without HDR metadata; transfer-only HDR gate returns before copying hinted peak to returned target color.
Absent LINEAR target peak infers nominal1=203 nits.
HDR metadata constructor uses opticalOutputScale1; constructor runs for preceding PQ swapchain.
BT2020_LINEAR assigns extendedLinearITUR2020 and EDRtrue; it neither rescales components nor clears prior EDRMetadata.
Public documented float relationship C=opticalOutputScale*y; normalized formats instead assume10000.
mpv screenshot renders separately toUNORM and clearsLINEAR source max_luma, so screenshot output is not a direct native-swapchain readback.

provenance.sourceScope: Uncommitted standalone diagnostics only. Final source corresponds to fresh-scale build; earlier host binaries precede the later control additions and are identified by their own wrapper hashes. App/core/shared remain unchanged within and across all three controls. Existing PiPBufferSnapshot used only for raw metadata/pixel serialization; no AVKit renderer or PiP controller instantiated.
